_comment: How big a generated set's scenery may be before it is scaled down. Read by ToonBackdropScale at save time; the binary carries clamped _fallback_only copies. These are PERCEPTUAL numbers — the camera shows about 1.8 stage units across and 1.0 tall, so a 1.7-unit cottage technically fits and still fills the entire screen. Found by rendering, not by reasoning, which is why they live here and not in Swift.
_standsUpAbove_comment: A shape whose top is below this is scenery lying on the ground — a path, a hill line, a kerb — and is never a scale candidate. Ground planes and sky bands MUST keep spanning x=-3..3 so a camera move never reveals an edge.
_bandWidth_comment: Reach, not width, separates a band from a building: something spanning the whole stage AND standing tall is a wall of sky, not a house, and scaling it is the one change that actually breaks a backdrop.
